title: What the joining policy builds when the fresh count is free
claim: T1: with no stall, the parity pattern grown by CUBIC-FROM-A-KNOT's policy with any count rule is the rank-truncated distributive lattice of ideals of the descent order of its offshoots (Birkhoff); groups are lower covers of the next size's ideals, demand = minimal offshoots outside, surplus = new offshoots; a count below demand stalls; implied parity iff demand 0. T2: one count c for every join survives iff c = a (seed size), building N^a; else stalls at rounds 2 / 4 / 3. T3: with groups of at most three, only c = a = 3; capped = uncapped iff no ideal has four maximal elements. T4: fewest counts close one knot into the 2^a pattern and stop; from any hand-over they conserve the chains with demand 1; the crossed start keeps a chains for every a. T5: bond balls of N^a are Theta(r^a), a >= 3. T6: the threshold reader recovers every junction of the uniform growth, a >= 3.
standard_statement: Birkhoff's representation (finitary form, Stanley EC1 Prop. 3.4.3); conflict-free prime event structures (Nielsen-Plotkin-Winskel 1981); cube condition of median graphs (Barthelemy-Constantin 1993; Chepoi 2000); order dimension = width of join-irreducibles (Dilworth 1950); minimal cuts connected when short cycles generate (Babson-Benjamini 1999; Timar 2013).
